newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus parliament awards Ford tax breaks.
newsitem.headline: Belarus parliament awards Ford tax breaks.

text.p: The Belarussian parliament approved tax and customs exemptions on Friday for a Ford Motor Co joint venture factory due to begin production on July 31.
The upper house approved a lower house decision by 38 to seven to free Ford from paying customs and excise duties and value added tax (VAT) on imported parts for an unlimited period.
It also freed the joint venture from tax for five years on profits generated at the 6,000 annual capacity plant outside the capital Minsk.
Ford's $19.2 million investment gives it a 51 percent stake in the venture, which it has refurbished. The government has a 26 percent for land and buildings and local partner Lada OMC has 23 percent.
The plant in Belarus, conveniently located between Central Europe and Russia, is Ford's entry point into the Russian market which is expected to boom in coming years.
Belarus and Russia have a number of customs agreements which will allow Ford to ship to Russia and avoid some taxes.

Some Belarus deputies opposed the new law. "Domestic producers will not understand giving subsidies like that to a foreign enterprise," the Economy, Budget and Finance Committee head Mikhail Matusevich told parliament.
Ford has a 99-year lease of the site and an option to expand it if it wants to build a body shop and paint shop, Neil Campbell, General Director of Ford's Belarus operation, told Reuters recently.
Ford plans to hold an opening ceremony on July 30 at the plant, which it says will employ about 150 people directly and 200 contractors.
